n: Unlike the other friends, Elihu calls Job by name and asks him personally to listen.

f.g: Elihu is the only speaker besides God to address Job by name.

n: He has opened his mouth and is ready to speak.

f.w: my tongue hath spoken in my mouth
f.g: A formal way of saying “I am about to speak.”

n: He promises his words will come from an honest heart and state knowledge plainly.

f.g: Sincerity, honest intent.

n: Elihu, like Job, owes his life to God’s Spirit and breath. They stand on equal footing.

f.w: The Spirit of God hath made me

n: If Job can answer him, let him prepare his arguments and take his stand.

f.g: Prepare your case.

n: Elihu says he is the kind of go-between Job wanted — a fellow mortal made from clay, speaking for God.

f.g: As God’s spokesman — or “I am just like you before God.”

n: Since he is only human, Job need not be terrified of him, as he feared being overwhelmed by God (9:34; 13:21).

f.w: my terror shall not make thee afraid

n: Elihu quotes what he has heard Job say.

f.w: I have heard the voice of thy words
f.g: Elihu summarizes Job’s claims, though not always precisely.

n: Job claimed to be pure and innocent. (Job had said he was blameless, but he never claimed to be completely sinless — see 7:21; 13:26.)
And Job said God invents excuses to attack him and treats him as an enemy.

f.w: he counteth me for his enemy

n: God, Job said, puts his feet in the stocks and watches every step.

f.g: A wooden frame that locked a prisoner’s feet.

n: Elihu answers: in this Job is wrong, because God is greater than any human being.
Why does Job complain that God won’t answer him? God does not have to give account of everything he does.

f.w: he giveth not account of any of his matters
f.g: Or “he does not answer all a man’s words.”

n: Elihu’s key point: God does speak, in one way and then another, but people don’t notice.
One way God speaks is through dreams and night visions while people sleep.

f.w: In a dream, in a vision of the night

n: He opens their ears and seals his warnings in their minds.

f.g: Stamps his warning on them, like a seal on a document.

n: His purpose is to turn people away from wrong plans and to cut away their pride.

f.g: Remove pride from a person.

n: God does this to rescue them from the grave and from crossing the river of death.

f.g: The grave or realm of the dead.
Possibly “crossing the river” of death.

n: A second way God speaks: through pain and illness, chastening someone on a sickbed. This is a new idea in the debate — suffering as teaching, not just punishment.

f.g: Disciplined, corrected.

n: The sick person loses his appetite even for the finest food.

f.g: Delicious food, delicacies.

n: His body wastes away until his bones stick out.

f.w: his bones that were not seen stick out

n: He draws near to the grave and to the messengers of death.

f.g: Angels of death.

n: But if there is a messenger — an angel or mediator, one in a thousand — to speak for him and show what is right…

f.w: a messenger with him, an interpreter
f.g: Hebrew mal’ak (angel/messenger) and melits (mediator, interpreter).

n: …then God is gracious and says, “Spare him from the pit — I have found a ransom.” Many Christians read this as pointing to the ransom Christ paid for all.

f.g: Hebrew kopher — a price paid to set someone free; related to the word for atonement.

n: His body becomes fresh as a child’s, and he is restored to the strength of youth.
He prays and God accepts him. He sees God’s face with joy, and God restores him to a right relationship.

f.w: he shall see his face with joy

n: He sings before others, “I sinned and twisted what was right, but I was not repaid as I deserved.” This is confession and grace.

f.g: Better “I was not punished as I deserved.”

n: God redeems him from the pit, and he lives to see the light.

f.w: his life shall see the light

n: God works like this again and again with people.

f.g: Literally “twice, three times” — repeatedly.

n: His purpose is always to bring people back from death into the light of life.
Elihu asks Job to pay attention and stay quiet while he continues.

f.g: Be silent.

n: If Job has something to say, he should speak — Elihu genuinely wants to see him cleared.

f.g: I want to see you vindicated.

n: If not, Job should listen and Elihu will teach him wisdom.
